decision_conditions: The conversion of the existing three-bedroom dwelling into a 6 bed HMO would result in the loss of a residential unit that is suitable and appropriately sized for a family. The proposal would therefore unacceptably undermine the supply of family housing within the Borough for which there is an identified need, contrary to Policies DMH 1 and DMH 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy H10 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed development, by reason of the increased number of independent occupiers associated with a six person HMO, would generate materially greater levels of noise, comings and goings, and garden use than the existing C3 dwelling, resulting in unacceptable disturbance to neighbouring residents. No Management Plan or Planning Statement has been submitted to demonstrate how these impacts would be appropriately managed or mitigated, particularly in relation to noise control, refuse management, garden use, and the day to day operation of the HMO. In the absence of such information, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the intensified use could operate without causing harm to neighbouring amenity. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D13 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 135(f) of the NPPF (2024).

The ground floor rear bedroom would receive poor levels of outlook and privacy, with its only window and door facing directly onto the communal garden with no defensible space, resulting in a high likelihood of direct overlooking from other occupants using this area. Access to this room is also taken directly from the communal kitchen/living area, exposing future occupiers to unacceptable levels of noise and disturbance from the only communal living space. This arrangement would fail to provide a comfortable, private or functionally acceptable living environment. The proposal therefore conflicts with Policies DMH 5, DMHB 11 and DMHB 16 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 135(f) of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed development, by reason of its insufficient car parking provision, would lead to overspill parking on the public highway, resulting in increased obstruction, vehicle conflict and associated highway safety risks. No parking stress survey or Transport Statement  has been submitted to justify this shortfall. Given the site's low PTAL rating and the presence of both a CPZ and unrestricted parking nearby, the development would likely result in overspill parking, increased congestion and highway safety risks. In the absence of evidence demonstrating that these impacts can be mitigated, the proposal is contrary to  Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 116 of the NPPF (2024).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
description: Erection of a part single, part two storey extension to the rear, conversion of Class C3 dwelling to Class C4 HMO
